newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open slightly weaker, underperform.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open slightly weaker, underperform.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened slightly weaker in a quiet market on Friday, underperforming U.S. Treasuries, as weakness in the Canadian dollar weighed on prices, analysts said.
"Canada is holding up fairly well in light of the dollar weakness," said Mary Jane Yule, a senior portfolio manager with Jones Heward Investment Counsel Inc. "It seems very quiet."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.05 to C$108.60 to yield 7.260 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 5/32 to yield 7.05 percent. The spread between the two bonds widened to 21 basis points from 19 basis points on Thursday.

"It's probably the modest impact of the dollar. And also our spreads over the last little while have really narrowed in quite a bit," said Yule. "We have outperformed over the last week or so. It's just unwinding a bit of that."

The Canadian dollar continued to languish at lower levels on Friday as it met with further selling by U.S. accounts. The unit opened at C$1.4009 (US$0.7138) against a close of C$1.3998 (US$0.7144) and hit a low of C$1.4024 overnight.
The Canadian dollar has weakened to two-year lows in recent weeks amid concern that a near-term rise in U.S. interest rates would not be matched by the Bank of Canada, analysts said.

Canadian and U.S. bond investors this morning are also looking ahead to the release the of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index. The index is the only major piece of economic data being released this morning in either country.
In new issue news, the Government of Canada on Thursday said it plans to auction on April 23 C$1.3 billion of bonds with a coupon of 8.0 percent and maturing June 1, 2027.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.03 to C$102.07 to yield 6.703 percent.
The U.S. bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 13 basis points from 15 basis points on Thursday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.22 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.28 percent.
